rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and reveal the overall retention window and critical pairs without undue risk of truncation.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the best next move is to shorten the gradient to reduce t_last and improve CRF while keeping the same broad window and temperature. A moderate step from 20 to 16 min should test how much speed we can gain before the 6/7 region becomes limiting.

We are very close to the optimum, with full resolution and only a small time penalty left, so the next step is to shorten the gradient one more increment. The 6/7 pair is now the limiting pair, and this run will show whether we can get t_last under 10 min without dropping below R = 1.5.

At 14 min the only loss is the 6/7 pair, so keep the faster gradient and lower temperature one step to increase selectivity and recover that critical resolution while staying under the 10 min target if possible.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity, so return to 40 C and instead narrow the gradient window slightly by reducing phi1 to 0.90. This should make the gradient effectively shallower around the crowded mid-elution region and may recover the 6/7 resolution while keeping the run near the 10 min target.

Reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the limiting 6/7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. A slightly narrower gradient window may push that pair to full credit while still avoiding a time penalty.

At phi1 0.85 the critical pair is fully resolved but t_last is slightly too long, so the next move is to shorten tG one step to pull the last peak back under 10 min. This tests whether we can keep the improved selectivity from the narrower window while removing the small time penalty.

The best region appears to be near phi1 0.90, and selectivity improves with a slightly shallower gradient, so test tG 16 min at phi1 0.90. This should increase the limiting 6/7 resolution from the 14 min run, and if t_last stays close enough to 10 min it may outperform the current best.

The current best is very close to full score, needing only a modest boost to the 6/7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min. Raising temperature one step at the best phi1/tG setting probes whether selectivity around that critical pair improves without pushing the last peak too late.

The best unresolved tradeoff is between 0.90/14 (good time, slightly low R) and 0.85/14 (full R, slight time penalty), so test the intermediate effect via a shallower gradient at phi1 0.85. This may preserve full resolution and reveal whether the extra selectivity is enough to justify the modest retention increase.

The optimum appears near phi1 0.90, tG 14, T 40, with only the 6/7 pair slightly under-resolved; changing temperature was harmful, so now test a higher phi0 to reshape the early-to-mid gradient slope while keeping the endpoint and run time favorable. This may selectively open the crowded middle region enough to reach full credit without pushing t_last past 10 min.

Injection 11 is the best yet and only narrowly misses full credit on the 6/7 pair, so reduce phi1 one step while keeping phi0, tG, and T fixed. This should slightly flatten the gradient in the crowded region and may lift that pair above R = 1.5, with a good chance of keeping t_last at or near 10 min.

We have reached full score, so the only worthwhile exploration is whether a faster method can still keep every pair at R >= 1.5 and t_last within 10 min. Shortening tG by one step tests the speed limit around the current optimum; if it fails, injection 12 remains the method to keep.

Since 12 min was too fast, keep tG at 14 min and test whether narrowing the window one more step can still maintain full resolution while pulling the method just onto the favorable side of the 10 min boundary. This directly probes whether there is an equally scoring but slightly more selective operating point adjacent to the optimum.

Injection 12 is optimal in score, but a small increase in phi0 could slightly accelerate the late peak while preserving the favorable narrower window and crowded-region selectivity. This tests whether the same full resolution can be retained with a bit more front-end strength and a safer margin on t_last.

Injection 15 matches the maximum score with a better time margin than injection 12, so it is the best platform for one more speed test. We already have a robust CRF 1.000 point at phi0 0.15, phi1 0.85, so the remaining useful check is the other side of that local optimum. Testing phi1 0.90 at the same phi0 will map whether 0.85 is truly centered as the best endpoint and confirm the local response around the winning method.

We have already mapped the main gradient-variable neighborhood around the two CRF 1.000 methods, so use one remaining shot to test temperature at the better-resolved phi0 0.10, phi1 0.85 condition. Temperature increases were clearly harmful, but we have not tested whether a lower temperature can retain the winning 0.15/0.85/14 shape while perhaps improving the 6/7 selectivity enough to give a more robust full-resolution margin. This is a local robustness check around the current best method.

Two methods already achieve CRF 1.000, so with the remaining budget the best use is boundary mapping around the faster 0.15/0.85/14/40 condition. Testing phi0 0.20 with phi1 0.80 checks whether the loss in 6/7 resolution at higher phi0 can be offset by a narrower window while keeping the run fast.

A third CRF 1.000 point at 0.20/0.80/14/40 suggests a ridge of optimal methods, so push one more step in phi0 to define its edge. This tests whether additional front-end strength can still preserve the critical 6/7 resolution while keeping the run fully within the 10 min target.

The 0.20/0.80/14/40 method is fully optimal and sits near the fast edge, so with two injections left the most informative final probe is to shorten tG one step there. This tests whether that higher-phi0, lower-phi1 optimum can run faster than 14 min while still holding the 6/7 pair above R = 1.5.

With one injection left and several CRF 1.000 methods already found, the most useful final probe is one more step narrower from the fully optimal 0.20/0.80/14/40 condition.
